title: Identities, roles, permissions
summary: Global accounts that can belong to several tenants, tenant administration by the platform super admin, memberships with internal or external account types, local authentication (Argon2id, reset by email), OIDC and TOTP MFA under a per-tenant authentication policy, secure cookie sessions holding a single tenant, groups, tenant-defined node roles as permission sets with a cached permission engine, the members and roles administration screens, the My account screen, and GDPR rights (personal data export, erasure by anonymization). Grants of roles on hierarchy nodes and their inheritance are delivered in L03; API tokens and the OAuth server in L15.

stories.title: Platform super admin manages tenants
stories.i_want: to create, configure and delete tenants
stories.so_that: each organization gets an isolated space with its own defaults
acceptance: Given I am super admin, When I create tenant `acme` with a default language, time zone, default capacity and overload tolerance, Then it is reachable at `acme.<domain>` (or the single domain in single-tenant mode)
Given a tenant exists, When I set its storage and API rate quotas, Then they are stored and exposed to the services that enforce them
Given a tenant, When I delete it after typing its key to confirm, Then all its data is removed in the background and its subdomain no longer resolves
Given a tenant admin who is not super admin, When they call the tenant management API, Then they get 403 Problem Details `forbidden`
Given single-tenant mode is configured, When the platform starts for the first time, Then a default tenant and an initial super admin are bootstrapped from environment variables

tech.title: Extend the tenant table with settings and quotas
tech.description: Add tenant settings: key/subdomain (unique), default language, time zone, default weekly capacity, overload tolerance, overload mode, quotas (storage, API rate), multi-tenant flag. Add a platform-level role marker on accounts for super admin, outside RLS.
done_when: Migration applies and rolls forward cleanly
Integration tests verify uniqueness of the tenant key and default values
Unit tests cover settings validation (time zone, tolerance range)

tech.title: Expose super admin tenant management endpoints
tech.description: Add `/api/v1/platform/tenants` endpoints (list, create, update, delete) restricted to super admin. Deletion enqueues a background purge job. Bootstrap command creates the default tenant and first super admin in single-tenant mode.
done_when: Unit tests cover authorization and validation rules
Integration tests cover create, update, delete and 403 for non super admins on real PostgreSQL
Purge job integration test proves no row of the deleted tenant remains

stories.title: Sign in with a local account and reset my password
stories.i_want: to sign in with my email and password and reset it by email if I forget it
stories.so_that: I can access my tenant securely without an external identity provider
acceptance: Given a valid email and password, When I sign in on `acme.<domain>`, Then a session cookie (`httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite`) is set for tenant Acme only
Given a wrong password, When I sign in 5 times in a row, Then further attempts are rate limited and the error never reveals whether the email exists
Given I requested a reset, When I open the emailed link within its validity, Then I can set a new password and all my other sessions are revoked
Given a state-changing request without a valid CSRF token, When it reaches the API, Then it is rejected with 403
Given I sign out, When I reuse the old cookie, Then the API answers 401

tech.title: Implement the SKIP LOCKED job queue in the worker
tech.description: Create the `job` table and a worker loop polling with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, retries with backoff, and per-job tenant context (`SET LOCAL`). First consumers: tenant purge and transactional emails. Reused by every later background job.
done_when: Unit tests cover retry and backoff computation
Integration tests with two worker instances prove each job is processed exactly once
Jobs run under the job's tenant RLS context

tech.title: Create account, membership and credential tables
tech.description: Create `account` (global, the only business table without `tenant_id`, unique verified email), `membership` (account, tenant, type internal/external, status, tenant roles) with RLS, and credentials with Argon2id hashes and password reset tokens (hashed, expiring).
done_when: Integration tests prove membership rows are isolated per tenant under RLS
Unit tests cover email normalization
CI RLS check whitelists only `account`

tech.title: Implement Argon2id authentication and Valkey sessions
tech.description: Implement sign-in, sign-out and session endpoints: Argon2id verification, sessions stored in Valkey holding a single tenant, secure cookie flags, CSRF double-submit token, rate limiting per IP and per email. The session extractor rejects accounts without an active membership in the resolved tenant.
done_when: Unit tests cover password hashing parameters and CSRF validation
Integration tests on real PostgreSQL and Valkey cover sign-in, wrong password, rate limit, sign-out and cross-tenant cookie reuse rejected
No user enumeration in error responses (asserted by tests)

tech.title: Send password reset emails through the job queue
tech.description: Add an email module in `infra` (SMTP, templated FR/EN messages in the tenant or user language) and a password reset flow: request endpoint, emailed signed single-use link, reset endpoint revoking other sessions.
done_when: Unit tests cover token expiry and single use
Integration tests use a local SMTP catcher to assert the email content and link
Reset revokes other sessions (asserted)

tech.title: Build the sign-in, forgot and reset password screens
tech.description: Build sign-in, forgot password and reset password pages in `projects/app` following the sign-in mockup: `mat-form-field appearance="outline"`, labelled fields, error messages from Problem Details codes via Transloco, loading and error states. Use the generated API client only.
done_when: Unit tests cover form validation and error mapping
Integration tests render each page against a mocked client
axe-core passes; all texts are Transloco keys in FR and EN

tech.title: Add e2e test for sign-in, sign-out and password reset
tech.description: Playwright test on the compose stack: sign in, reach the shell, sign out, request a reset, read the email from the SMTP catcher, set a new password and sign in again.
done_when: Test passes headless in CI
axe-core checks run on each page of the flow

stories.title: Two-step verification with an authenticator app
stories.i_want: to enable TOTP two-step verification with backup codes
stories.so_that: my account stays protected even if my password leaks
acceptance: Given I am signed in, When I enable two-step verification and confirm a valid TOTP code, Then MFA is active and 8 single-use backup codes are shown once
Given MFA is active, When I sign in with my password, Then I must enter a valid TOTP or backup code before a session is created
Given an invalid code entered repeatedly, When the limit is reached, Then attempts are rate limited
Given a used backup code, When I try it again, Then it is refused
Given the tenant policy requires MFA for local accounts, When a member without MFA signs in, Then they are forced to enroll before accessing the application

tech.title: Implement TOTP enrollment, verification and backup codes
tech.description: Store an encrypted TOTP secret per account and hashed backup codes. Add enrollment (secret + otpauth URI), confirmation, verification step in sign-in (pending-MFA session state) and disable endpoints. Use an MIT/Apache TOTP crate.
done_when: Unit tests cover TOTP window tolerance and backup code single use
Integration tests cover the full sign-in with MFA and rate limiting
Secrets are encrypted at rest with a key from a secret file

tech.title: Build the MFA challenge and enrollment screens
tech.description: Build the verification step of the sign-in flow and the enrollment dialog (QR code rendered locally, code confirmation, backup codes display with copy/download) using MatDialog and Material form fields.
done_when: Unit tests cover the step state machine
Integration tests render enrollment and challenge with mocked API
axe-core passes; QR code has a text alternative (secret key)

tech.title: Add e2e test for MFA enrollment and sign-in
tech.description: Playwright test enabling MFA (TOTP computed in the test), signing out, signing in with TOTP, then with a backup code.
done_when: Test passes headless in CI
axe-core checks run on each step

stories.title: Sign in through the tenant's OIDC provider and auth policy
stories.i_want: to configure an OIDC provider and an authentication policy for my tenant
stories.so_that: my users sign in with our corporate SSO and MFA is enforced where we require it
acceptance: Given I configure an OIDC provider (issuer, client ID, secret) for Acme, When a user clicks "Sign in with Entra ID", Then they are authenticated through the provider and their membership is matched by verified email
Given the policy "internal accounts must use SSO", When an internal member tries a password sign-in, Then it is refused with a message pointing to SSO
Given the policy "local accounts require MFA", When a local account signs in, Then MFA is required
Given an account member of tenants A and B with different policies, When they enter tenant B, Then B's policy applies
Given an OIDC callback with an invalid state or nonce, When it reaches the API, Then it is rejected

tech.title: Store per-tenant OIDC providers and authentication policy
tech.description: Create tables for OIDC provider configuration per tenant (issuer, client ID, encrypted secret, display name, email claim) and the authentication policy (SSO required for internal accounts, MFA required for local accounts, portal methods). RLS applies.
done_when: Integration tests prove isolation of provider configs between tenants
Unit tests cover policy evaluation for each account type
Client secrets encrypted at rest

tech.title: Implement the OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE
tech.description: Implement OIDC login and callback endpoints (discovery, PKCE, state, nonce, ID token validation) with an MIT/Apache crate, account matching by verified email, and policy enforcement at sign-in. Keycloak in the `sso` profile serves as the integration test provider.
done_when: Unit tests cover policy enforcement and ID token claim validation
Integration tests against Keycloak cover success, invalid state and policy refusals
SAML/LDAP documented as handled through Keycloak

tech.title: Build the authentication administration tab
tech.description: Build the "Authentication" tab of the administration screen: OIDC provider form, policy toggles (`mat-slide-toggle`), test connection action, and the SSO buttons on the sign-in page driven by the tenant configuration.
done_when: Unit tests cover form validation
Integration tests render the tab and the sign-in page with and without providers
axe-core passes; all labels are Transloco keys

stories.title: Belong to several tenants and switch between them
stories.i_want: to see the tenants I belong to and switch the active one
stories.so_that: I can work for several organizations with a single account
acceptance: Given I am a member of Acme and Acme Services, When I open the tenant switcher, Then I see both with my role in each
Given I switch to Acme Services, When the switch completes, Then a new session for that tenant is established under its authentication policy and no Acme data is visible
Given an external (portal-only) membership, When that account calls any internal application endpoint, Then the API answers 403 whatever its role
Given I am not a member of a tenant, When I open its subdomain, Then I cannot sign in to it

tech.title: Expose my memberships and tenant switch endpoints
tech.description: Add `/api/v1/me` and `/api/v1/me/memberships` (read across tenants through a dedicated, audited query path that only returns the caller's memberships) and a switch endpoint that issues a session for the target tenant after applying its policy. Enforce the external-account restriction in the shared request layer.
done_when: Unit tests cover the external account guard
Integration tests cover switching, policy re-evaluation and 403 for external accounts on internal endpoints
Cross-tenant test proves no data from the previous tenant is reachable after switching

tech.title: Implement the tenant switcher in the shell
tech.description: Implement the organization selector in the navigation drawer (mat-select) and the "My organizations" card, redirecting to the target subdomain or re-establishing the session. Clear all client state on switch.
done_when: Unit tests cover state reset on switch
Integration tests render the switcher with one and several memberships
axe-core passes

stories.title: Invite and manage tenant members and groups
stories.i_want: to invite members, set their account type and tenant role, and organize them in groups
stories.so_that: the right people get access and permissions can be granted to groups
acceptance: Given I am tenant admin, When I invite `p.durand@client.example` as external, Then an invitation email is sent and the member appears as "Invitation sent"
Given the members list, When I filter by internal or external or pending invitations and search by name or email, Then the table shows matching members with type, tenant role, groups, MFA and status
Given a member, When I change their tenant role to configuration admin, Then they can manage configurations but not members
Given a group "Platform", When I add and remove members, Then group membership is updated and audited
Given a configuration admin, When they try to invite a member, Then they get 403
Given I remove a member from the tenant, When they next call the API, Then their sessions for this tenant are rejected

tech.title: Create invitation, group and group member tables
tech.description: Create `invitation` (tenant, email, type, role, token hash, expiry, status), `group` and `group_member` with RLS and indexes starting with `tenant_id`.
done_when: Integration tests verify RLS isolation of groups and invitations
Unit tests cover invitation expiry
Unique group name per tenant enforced

tech.title: Implement member, invitation and group endpoints
tech.description: Add endpoints to list and search members (cursor pagination), invite, accept an invitation (creating or linking a global account), change type and tenant role, remove a member (revoking sessions) and manage groups. Restricted to tenant admins; configuration admins are refused.
done_when: Unit tests cover role checks for tenant admin vs configuration admin
Integration tests cover invite, accept, change role, remove with session revocation, and cross-tenant isolation
Invitation email sent through the job queue (SMTP catcher assertion)

tech.title: Build the Members and Groups administration tabs
tech.description: Build the administration screen with `mat-tab-nav-bar` (Members, Groups, Roles, Authentication, Project configurations, Quotas). Members tab: search field, filter chips, invite dialog, `mat-table` with type and status chips. Groups tab: list, create, edit members. Loading, empty and error states.
done_when: Unit tests cover filters and the invite dialog form
Integration tests render tabs with mocked client data
axe-core passes; table is keyboard navigable

tech.title: Add e2e test for inviting and accepting a member
tech.description: Playwright test: tenant admin invites an internal member, the invitee opens the email link, sets a password and lands in the application; then the admin removes them and access is lost.
done_when: Test passes headless in CI
axe-core checks run on the admin screen

stories.title: Define node roles as sets of permissions
stories.i_want: to define node roles such as "Project manager" by toggling permissions
stories.so_that: permissions match how my organization works and can be granted on hierarchy nodes
acceptance: Given I am tenant admin, When I create role "Project manager" with view, create ticket, edit, comment, log time, assign resources, force overload and manage sprints, Then the role is saved with those permissions
Given a role, When I edit its labels in French and English, Then the labels are stored as translatable JSONB and shown in the user's language
Given a role used by grants, When I change its permissions, Then the permission cache is invalidated and the change applies within seconds
Given a role used by grants, When I try to delete it, Then I am told how many grants use it and deletion is refused
Given an endpoint protected by permission `comment`, When a user without it calls it, Then the API answers 403 with a stable code

tech.title: Define the permission catalog and role model in the domain
tech.description: Define in `crates/domain` the fixed permission catalog (view, create ticket, edit, comment, log time, assign resources, force overload, manage sprints, manage members, administer node, plus later permissions) as stable identifiers, the role entity and the effective-permission computation interface used by L03 inheritance.
done_when: Unit tests cover permission set operations (union, contains)
Integration test not applicable to pure domain code; covered through T02 endpoints
Catalog exported in OpenAPI as an enum

tech.title: Implement role tables, endpoints and the cached permission check
tech.description: Create `role` table (translatable labels JSONB, permission list) with RLS, CRUD endpoints for tenant admins, and a permission check middleware/helper with a Valkey cache invalidated by events. Seed default roles per new tenant.
done_when: Unit tests cover the check helper and cache key building
Integration tests on PostgreSQL and Valkey cover CRUD, deletion refusal when used, cache invalidation and 403 responses
Cross-tenant test proves roles are not visible across tenants

tech.title: Build the Roles tab with permission toggles
tech.description: Build the Roles tab: role list, role detail panel with a `mat-slide-toggle` per permission (labels from Transloco), FR/EN label fields, create, duplicate and delete actions with confirmation dialog.
done_when: Unit tests cover dirty state and save
Integration tests render a role and toggle permissions with mocked client
axe-core passes; every toggle has an accessible label

stories.title: Manage my account: preferences, sessions and security
stories.i_want: to set my language and time zone, change my password, manage MFA and my active sessions
stories.so_that: the application fits me and I control access to my account
acceptance: Given I set my language to English and time zone to Europe/Paris, When I reload, Then texts are in English and timestamps are shown in Paris time
Given I change my password with my current password, When it succeeds, Then my other sessions are revoked
Given the active sessions list, When I revoke a device, Then that session is rejected on its next request
Given MFA is active, When I disable it, Then I must confirm with a valid code, unless the tenant policy requires MFA in which case disabling is refused

tech.title: Implement preferences, password change and session endpoints
tech.description: Add account preferences (language, time zone) on the global account, password change, list and revoke sessions (device, last activity) stored in Valkey.
done_when: Unit tests cover time zone validation and session listing
Integration tests cover password change revoking other sessions and individual session revocation
Policy-required MFA cannot be disabled (asserted)

tech.title: Build the My account screen
tech.description: Build the My account page: Preferences card (language, time zone selects applied immediately), Security card (MFA toggle, sessions dialog, password change dialog), My organizations card. The API tokens and authorized applications cards are added in L15.
done_when: Unit tests cover preference application to Transloco and date formatting
Integration tests render the page with mocked client
axe-core passes

stories.title: GDPR: export my data and erase accounts by anonymization
stories.i_want: to export my personal data and request the erasure of my account
stories.so_that: my GDPR rights of access and erasure are respected
acceptance: Given I am signed in, When I click "Export (JSON)", Then I download a JSON file with my account, memberships, preferences and the content I authored
Given I confirm erasure of my global account, When it completes, Then my name, email and avatar are removed and I appear as "Deleted user #1234" everywhere, history included
Given a tenant admin removes and erases a member, When erasure runs, Then only that tenant's membership is anonymized and the global account is untouched
Given the erasure option "purge comments", When it is chosen, Then the user's comments are deleted, otherwise content is kept
Given technical logs with IP addresses, When they are older than the configured retention (6 months by default), Then they are purged

tech.title: Implement personal data export and anonymization jobs
tech.description: Implement an export job producing JSON (downloadable via a short-lived link) and an anonymization job replacing personal data by a stable pseudonym `Deleted user #N` across all tenants (super admin or self) or one tenant (tenant admin), with optional comment purge. Design an extension point so later tables (comments, history) register their anonymization step.
done_when: Unit tests cover pseudonym generation and scope rules
Integration tests prove no personal field remains after erasure and that other tenants are untouched for tenant-scoped erasure
Every erasure is audited

tech.title: Expose export and erasure endpoints with confirmation
tech.description: Add endpoints for self export, self erasure (with re-authentication), tenant admin member erasure and super admin global erasure, plus a scheduled purge of technical logs with IPs after the configured retention.
done_when: Unit tests cover authorization per actor
Integration tests cover each actor and re-authentication requirement
Retention purge integration test removes old log rows only

tech.title: Build the My personal data card and erasure dialog
tech.description: Build the "My personal data" card: export button with progress and download, erasure dialog explaining consequences, requiring password (or SSO re-auth) and typed confirmation.
done_when: Unit tests cover the confirmation form
Integration tests render the card and dialog with mocked client
axe-core passes
